[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Governance decisions made without operational evidence are slow to detect problems and unable to demonstrate objective justification for interventions. Without a telemetry-to-governance feedback loop, poor-performing capabilities persist and the portfolio optimization cycle is disconnected from operational reality.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Connect operational metrics to governance actions: define metric thresholds that trigger governance reviews, contain or promote capabilities through an approved workflow, and feed monthly and quarterly governance reviews with scorecards built from the mandatory telemetry metrics.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- For all Production AI agents — feedback loops must be active during the full Production lifecycle
- When a governance decision (contain, restore, promote, retire) must be traceable to an objective operational signal
- When monthly or quarterly governance reviews lack objective data to drive portfolio decisions
page_texts.7:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Governance decisions are traceable to operational evidence, not anecdote
- Problems are detected early through threshold-triggered alerts rather than user escalations
- Portfolio optimization actions are driven by usage and quality trends rather than accumulated complaints
page_texts.9:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

AI governance committees and portfolio reviews typically receive periodic reports. Without a structured telemetry-to-governance feedback path, the reports are backward-looking and incomplete. Governance actions depend on who raised a concern rather than on what the data shows. High-performing capabilities are not promoted based on evidence, and low-performing ones persist because no objective trigger exists to require a decision.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The M365 Copilot platform provides some native analytics (usage volume, user adoption). For metrics not available natively (rework rate, policy compliance incidents), supplemental manual tracking processes are required. The mandatory metrics defined in STD-TEC-AI-006 provide the telemetry layer. This pattern defines how those metrics connect to governance actions.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Without a telemetry-to-governance feedback loop:
- Defect spikes are discovered through user escalations, not through systematic monitoring
- Policy compliance incidents may go undetected for weeks or months until an audit or complaint
- Governance reviews discuss capability quality based on verbal summaries rather than scorecard data
- Portfolio rationalization decisions lack objective usage data, making them vulnerable to appeal based on subjective advocacy
page_texts.12:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Metric collection for some signals (rework rate, policy compliance incidents) requires supplemental manual process tracking on the M365 platform — automated collection is not always available
- Threshold values for alerting must be defined numerically before Production promotion; subjective thresholds do not trigger consistent governance actions
- Governance actions triggered by telemetry still require human decision and approval — the feedback loop informs the decision but does not automate it
page_texts.14:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

Establish three feedback connections between telemetry and governance:

1. **Threshold-triggered alerts** — define numeric alert thresholds for defect rate and policy compliance incident count. When a threshold is crossed, an alert is generated to the domain owner and Platform Governance Team. The alert triggers a governance review within a defined response window, not an automated action.

2. **Governance workflow execution** — governance actions triggered by telemetry (contain, restore, promote, retire) are executed through an approved workflow when automation is available, or through a documented manual review queue when it is not. The key requirement is that the action is taken within a defined response time and is traceable to the triggering metric event.

3. **Scorecard-driven governance reviews** — monthly and quarterly governance reviews consume scorecard reports built from the mandatory metrics per STD-TEC-AI-006. Decisions made in these reviews are documented with the metric evidence that informed them.

[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Telemetry collection | Provides the mandatory metric data | STD-TEC-AI-006 |
| Alert thresholds | Define numeric trigger conditions for defect and compliance alerts | STD-TEC-AI-006 |
| Alert routing | Routes triggered alerts to domain owner and Platform Governance Team | STD-TEC-AI-006 |
| Governance review queue | Manual or automated review queue for threshold-triggered governance actions | STD-GOV-AI-004 (lifecycle state change), STD-GOV-AI-005 (rationalization) |
| Monthly domain scorecard | Aggregated mandatory metrics per domain for monthly review | STD-TEC-AI-006 |
| Quarterly enterprise scorecard | Aggregated mandatory metrics across all domains for quarterly review | STD-TEC-AI-006 |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Capability collects the seven mandatory metrics per STD-TEC-AI-006 continuously in Production
2. Metric values are evaluated against defined alert thresholds
3. When a threshold is crossed: alert is routed to domain owner and Platform Governance Team; a governance review is opened with a defined response window
4. Governance reviewer and domain owner assess the triggering metrics and produce a governance decision (contained, remediation plan, no action required)
5. Decisions and their triggering metric evidence are documented in the capability change log
6. Monthly domain scorecard aggregates mandatory metrics for the monthly domain hygiene review
7. Quarterly enterprise scorecard aggregates metrics for the quarterly consolidation review
page_texts.18:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Expedited human review**: when a policy compliance incident threshold is crossed, an immediate alert with highest-priority routing is generated to the domain owner and Platform Governance Team. For high-severity policy-compliance defects, per STD-TEC-AI-005, containment is triggered immediately and automatically upon threshold breach — it is not gated on prior human review. The expedited governance review (within a compressed response window, same business day) follows the automatic containment and determines remediation or restoration, with the decision and its rationale documented per STD-GOV-AI-004. For lower-severity compliance incidents that do not meet the immediate-containment criteria, containment still requires human review and approval before execution.
- **Lightweight version for limited telemetry environments**: when only usage volume and manual incident reports are available, the feedback loop operates through the monthly manual review process rather than continuous threshold monitoring
page_texts.20:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- All seven mandatory metrics per STD-TEC-AI-006 are being collected before Production promotion
- Alert thresholds are defined as specific numeric values before Production promotion
- Governance review queue process and response windows defined before Production promotion
page_texts.22:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#phase-1-threshold-and-alert-configuration]

#### Phase 1: Threshold and Alert Configuration

1. Define numeric alert thresholds for defect spikes and policy compliance incidents for each capability, using the Pilot period baseline to calibrate initial threshold values
2. Define escalation paths — who is notified, in what sequence, with what response time expectation, by incident severity tier
3. Define containment criteria — the threshold conditions that trigger a containment action
page_texts.23:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#phase-2-scorecard-configuration]

#### Phase 2: Scorecard Configuration

1. Define the monthly domain scorecard format: which metrics, at what aggregation level, in what format
2. Define the quarterly enterprise scorecard format
3. Assign responsibility for scorecard production to the Platform Governance Team
page_texts.24:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#phase-3-governance-review-integration]

#### Phase 3: Governance Review Integration

1. Confirm that governance reviews (monthly domain, quarterly enterprise) have scorecard data as the primary input for capability quality discussions
2. Establish the convention that all governance decisions on capability status must reference the metric evidence that informed the decision
page_texts.25:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Calibrate alert thresholds during the Pilot period — thresholds that are not calibrated to actual baseline values produce false positives (too many alerts) or delayed detection (thresholds too loose)
- Document all governance actions triggered by telemetry in the capability change log — traceability from metric event to governance decision to action is the audit evidence
- Report both scorecard findings and the governance actions taken in response to them — a scorecard that produces no documented decisions is not functioning as a feedback loop
page_texts.26:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- Collecting metrics but not connecting them to governance actions — data collected for reporting without action is theater, not governance
- Defining alert thresholds as qualitative ("unusually high") rather than numeric — qualitative thresholds cannot be consistently applied or audited
- Making governance decisions based on anecdote in reviews that have scorecard data available — if the data is present, it must be used

page_texts.34:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#scenario-1-defect-spike-detection]

#### Scenario 1: Defect spike detection

A capability's defect rate crosses the defined alert threshold. An alert routes to the domain owner and Platform Governance Team. The governance reviewer opens a review within the defined response window. The review finds that a recent prompt change introduced a regression. A change record is opened to revert the change. The revert action is documented with the threshold-breach metric event as the trigger.
page_texts.35:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#scenario-2-monthly-scorecard-driving-rationalization]

#### Scenario 2: Monthly scorecard driving rationalization

The monthly domain scorecard shows that two capabilities have had usage below the defined minimum threshold for three consecutive months. The domain hygiene review opens rationalization reviews for both capabilities, citing the usage metric data. One capability is retired (no active users confirmed), and the other is contained pending an owner assignment.
page_texts.37:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

Governance reviews discuss capability quality based on verbal summaries and individual team reports. Problems are raised through user complaints. No standard metric set is available across capabilities. Governance decisions cannot be traced to evidence.
page_texts.38:
[patterns/governance/ai-development/PTN-GOV-AI-011-telemetry-to-governance-feedback-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

Governance reviews consume monthly and quarterly scorecards built from mandatory metrics. Threshold breaches trigger governance actions with defined response windows. All governance decisions reference the metric evidence that informed them and are documented in the capability change log.

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Governance decisions disconnected from operational evidence are slow to detect problems and unable to demonstrate objective justification.

**Solution:** Connect mandatory telemetry metrics to three feedback paths: threshold-triggered alerts, governance workflow execution, and scorecard-driven governance reviews — so that all portfolio decisions are traceable to operational evidence.

**When to Use:** All Production AI agents; monthly and quarterly governance reviews; any governance decision requiring objective justification.

**Key Benefits:**
- Governance decisions are traceable to operational evidence
- Problems detected through threshold alerts before user escalations
- Portfolio optimization driven by usage and quality trends

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** All seven mandatory metrics collected, alert thresholds defined numerically, governance review scorecard format established

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-012 Federated Change Gateway, PTN-GOV-AI-009 Portfolio Rationalization, PTN-TEC-AI-006 Degraded Evidence
